title: Relocating popular schools and social mixing in schools
asked: Mr David Hoe asked whether the Ministry of Education would periodically relocate popular schools to neighbourhoods with different housing and socioeconomic status mixes, to better align school access with meritocracy and social mixing.
answered_by: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
response: The Minister said MOE plans school places to meet national and local demand, taking into account current and projected school-going populations and nearby school supply. When demand falls or is projected to fall, MOE will consider relocating schools, including popular schools, to areas with higher demand, usually where significant new housing is being developed. MOE will continue to review admissions policies so schools remain accessible to children from all backgrounds. In supplementary answers, he described social mixing benefits and examples including the MOE-OBS Challenge, combined school CCAs, an RI boarding programme, and Phase 2C places ring-fenced on proximity.

key_points.point: MOE's main objective in planning schools is to meet national and localised demand for school places.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) main objective is to ensure that national as well as localised demand for school places are met

key_points.point: MOE considers current and projected school-going populations in each residential area and the supply of places from nearby schools.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: We take into account several factors, including current and projected school-going populations in each residential area, as well as the supply of places provided by the schools in the vicinity.

key_points.point: When demand falls or is projected to fall, MOE will consider relocating schools, including popular schools, to areas with higher demand.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: When the demand for school places falls or is projected to fall in a particular area, we will consider relocating schools in that area, including popular schools, to areas with higher demand.

key_points.point: Relocation usually targets areas where significant new housing is being developed, so schools serve new residents.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: These are usually areas where significant new housing is being developed and the schools will then serve the new residents moving into those areas.

key_points.point: MOE will continue to review admissions policies so schools remain accessible to children from all backgrounds.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: MOE will continue to review our school admissions policies so that our schools continue to remain accessible to children from all backgrounds.

key_points.point: Social mixing in schools is described as creating the environment and opportunity, through diverse student backgrounds, for holistic development.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: social mixing in our schools creates the environment as well as the opportunity with the diversity of students' backgrounds, to enable holistic development of our children

key_points.point: The MOE-OBS Challenge brings Secondary 3 students from different schools together to explore the outdoors.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: Secondary 3 students across different schools, living together, coming together over a period of time to explore the outdoors

key_points.point: Combined school CCAs include a girls' football team formed by Boon Lay Secondary School, Methodist Girls' School and Westwood Secondary School.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: Boon Lay Secondary School, Methodist Girls' School, as well as Westwood Secondary School

key_points.point: Raffles Institution runs a boarding programme with students from other secondary schools.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: Raffles Institution (RI) has a RI boarding programme

key_points.point: Phase 2C ring-fences a certain number of primary school places for children regardless of links or affiliation, based on proximity.
key_points.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
key_points.quote: a certain number of places is ring-fenced for children, regardless of whether they have any links or affiliation to the school or not, premise on the basis of proximity.

left_open: Whether popular schools would be periodically relocated specifically to areas with different housing and socioeconomic status mixes.
Use of administrative data on primary school intake by housing type to identify schools with little or no public housing within a two-kilometre radius.
Whether social mixing measures would be prioritised for schools with little or no public housing within a two-kilometre radius.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on social mixing in schools, opportunities beyond OBS, and using housing data to target social mixing measures.
